name: Rasuwa flood
where: Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and downstream, Nepal
headline: Rasuwa flood, live
lede: A flash flood came down the Bhote Koshi from Tibet into Rasuwa on 26 August 2026. Here is what is confirmed, what is still unknown, and who to call.
asOfSource: Nepal Police bulletin (bodies found as of 6am Saturday); NDRRMA, missing and China figures unchanged since Friday evening / Saturday morning

stats.label: confirmed dead
stats.detail: Nepal Police raised the toll to 616 bodies found, in a bulletin posted on its own website giving the count as of 6am Saturday, up from 553 in Friday's 5pm bulletin. The new district breakdown sums to 616: Chitwan 233, Nawalparasi East 158, Gorkha 48, Nawalparasi West 47, Dhading 45, Nuwakot 41, Tanahun 31, Rasuwa 13. The bulletin does not restate injured, rescued or missing figures, which still stand at their last published counts. Sources differ on whether this counts deaths on the China side, where state media (Xinhua) had the toll at 7 as of Saturday morning, so it is not added here.

stats.label: listed missing in Nepal
stats.detail: NDRRMA said in a Friday evening Search, Rescue and Relief update that 1,924 people are now listed out of contact in Nepal, nearly double the 977 it had given that same afternoon, up from 910 the evening before that. NDRRMA said the rise came from adding more local residents to the list, not a new wave of people going missing. The count of foreign nationals held at 517, unchanged. This figure is NDRRMA's, not the police's. Out of contact does not mean dead: phone lines, power and internet are still down across the valley.

stats.label: missing on the China side
stats.detail: Xinhua, China's state news agency, reports 554 people missing around Gyirong Port in Xizang (Tibet) as of Saturday morning, down slightly from the 558 Chinese media had given earlier, with 260 of them foreign nationals. Combined with Nepal's list that is more than 2,400 people unaccounted for across both countries, although the two countries' counts of foreign nationals may overlap.

stats.label: rescued so far
stats.detail: NDRRMA reports 113 people rescued from Timure, Dhunche, Syabrubesi, Uttargaya and Bidur: 88 Nepali citizens, 11 Indian, 8 Chinese, 4 Korean and 2 American. The authority has published their names. Nepal Police separately reported 1,545 people rescued in total as of its 7am bulletin on 28 August, reported by Onlinekhabar. NDRRMA itself told ABC News on Friday afternoon that 3,253 people had been rescued by helicopter across the flood zone, and its Friday evening update put that broader tally at about 3,742, a figure that has not been named or broken down. The Nepali Army said its helicopters had rescued 706 people by 3pm Friday, up from 449 at 12:20pm, including 40 foreign nationals (29 Indian, 4 German, 4 Chinese, 1 Omani and 2 South Korean), reported by Onlinekhabar. Nepal Tourism Board separately said 117 stranded tourists have been rescued from the Bhotekoshi area, reported by Onlinekhabar.

stats.label: hydropower projects damaged
stats.detail: The Nepal Electricity Authority reports 14 projects damaged with a combined capacity of about 748 MW: 9 operating plants (354 MW) and 5 under construction (394 MW). Named ones include Rasuwagadhi, Chilime, Sanjen Khola, Upper Trishuli-1, Trishuli and Devighat, plus a 220 kV substation. An earlier same-day Ministry of Energy estimate said 431 MW.

stats.label: since the flood
stats.detail: Counting from the morning of 26 August 2026, when the flood hit. Search, rescue and recovery work is still going on this many days later.

stats.label: damage, early estimate
stats.detail: Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal put damage to roads and bridges at about Rs 200 billion on 26 August, and called it preliminary. Hydropower and private property are not in that figure. The whole 42 km road from Betrawati to the Rasuwagadhi border crossing was destroyed at multiple points.

stats.label: relief money released
stats.detail: Rs 1 billion released by the government into the disaster relief fund, plus Rs 10 million each to Rasuwa and Nuwakot and Rs 5 million to Dhading. Public donations are not counted here until an official total is published.
